handbookNote: Missouri Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Missouri previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only mo_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Missouri Real Estate Commission (MREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading (via a plain curl -- pr.mo.gov did NOT block the request, unlike mass.gov's bot-blocking encountered for the Massachusetts build in this same campaign) and reading the official Missouri Real Estate Candidate Handbook (pr.mo.gov/boards/realestate/MOREP-handbook.pdf, copyright 2024, updated 7/18/2024). Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the handbook (page 11): Broker National portion = 90 items (100 points possible -- the handbook notes the National Broker exam includes questions scored up to two points), 150 minutes; Broker State portion = 75 items (75 points), 120 minutes; combined 270-minute time limit. Passing: 75% required on EACH portion independently. 5-10 unscored experimental items may also appear, counting against time. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=165, exam_duration_sec=16200 (270 min), pass_percent=75, min_correct=124 (each portion independently requires 75%: 90*0.75=67.5 rounded to 68 national + 75*0.75=56.25 rounded to 57 state = 125; using the combined-165-item single-number convention this site's track_registry schema requires, min_correct is set to ceil(165*0.75)=124 as the closest single-number approximation, consistent with how other multi-portion states in this campaign are modeled). NOTABLE: Missouri's total item count (165) and time limit (270 min) are meaningfully larger than every other state built in this campaign (NJ/TN/VA/MA were ~115-125 items; AZ was 180 but a single combined exam, not portion-split) -- Missouri splits its two, larger, independently-scored portions. CONTENT OUTLINE -- National portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the handbook, summing to exactly 100% of the 90-item national portion: Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-only sub-items), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-only supervisory sub-items), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to New Jersey's, Tennessee's, Virginia's, and Massachusetts's own PSI-published national-portion percentages for the Broker exam (see nj_re_broker.json, tn_re_broker.json, va_re_broker.json, ma_re_broker.json) -- further confirms PSI uses one shared multi-state 'National Portion' content-outline template for real estate broker exams nationwide, with only the State-specific portion varying meaningfully by state. Missouri State portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 75-item state portion, summing to exactly 75, page 14-15 of the handbook): Licenses 7 items (Applications for License, Qualification for Expiration and Renewal, Fictitious Name, Individual License/Business Name, Broker-Salesperson, Salesperson License, Partnership/Association/Corporate License), Educational Requirements 2 items (Continuing Education Requirements), Business Conduct and Practices 40 items -- by far the largest single state topic, over half the state portion (Improper Use of License and Office, Branch Office, Sales Manager, Clerical Personnel/Personal-Professional Assistants, Display of License, Advertising, Franchises/Trade Name/Insignia, Listings, Offers, Licensee's Interest in Transactions/Relationship with Parties, Escrow and Trust Accounts, Earnest Money/Disputes, Standard Forms, Closings and Closing Statements, Retention of Records, Commissions, Property Management, Closing an Office, Minimum Services), Disciplinary Proceedings 8 items (Complaints, Investigation, Violations, Action by the Commission, Action by the Administrative Hearing Commission, Penalty for Violating or Practicing without a License), Listing/Offer/and Closing Contract Forms and Costs 12 items, Brokerage Relationships 6 items (Disclosure of Agency, Types of Brokerage Relationships Permitted, Agency Duties and Responsibilities, Dual Agency). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights, not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported. Given the user's explicit instruction to scale up parallelism for this state specifically ('let's go all agents in one shot for the next state' / 'even 20 is good' / 'but all only for this state'), this bank was drafted across 19 parallel single-topic drafting passes (roughly one agent per individual real content-outline topic, a finer split than prior states' 6-multi-topic-bucket model), with the oversized 40-item Business Conduct and Practices state category further split across 4 of those 19 passes by natural sub-grouping (Office and Personnel Administration; Advertising and Franchises; Transactions, Escrow and Commissions; Records and Property Management) -- similar in spirit to how NJ's 30-item Statutes and Rules state bucket was split across 4 files in that earlier build. A CROSS-BUCKET DEDUP PASS found and resolved 6 genuine near-duplicates in the agency-disclosure/dual-agency-agreement statute cluster (RSMo 339.770/339.730/339.780), where the independently-assigned Brokerage Relationships (15) and Transactions/Escrow/Commissions (18) drafting passes both legitimately touched adjoining brokerage-agreement statutes -- resolved by keeping the copy in Brokerage Relationships (the topically-correct home per Missouri's own real content-outline sub-area 'Disclosure of Agency'/'Dual Agency') and removing the 6 duplicated items from the Transactions/Escrow/Commissions file (which included one same-file duplicate of its own, also removed). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_mo_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 19 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.1/24.9/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. All draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass, and were additionally run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) at build time to remove any further exact or near-duplicate items before loading. 826 raw questions drafted (832 before the manual dedup pass) against a 165-item exam -- a 5.01:1 pool ratio, comfortably clearing the standing 4:1 new-track floor with no backfill pass needed, the strongest ratio of any state in this campaign so far.
